source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN Examination, 7th ed.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: During a home visit, which finding needs counseling about injury risk?
questions.rationale: Stairs increase fall risk. A tucked-away cord and good lighting are not hazards.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q580 (PDF p. 785)
questions.quote: stairs are associated with an increased risk of falls.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which handwashing action shows a nursing attendant needs MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: Hands are kept lower than the forearms so water flows toward the fingertips.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q600 (PDF p. 809)
questions.quote: keeping the hands lower than the forearms so that water flows toward the fingertips.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client on partial weight-bearing uses crutches. How much weight may go on the affected leg?
questions.rationale: Partial weight-bearing allows 30% to 50% of body weight on the affected limb. Touchdown allows contact without weight.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q604 (PDF p. 815)
questions.quote: The client who has partial weight-bearing status is allowed to place 30% to 50% of the body weight on the affected limb.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which device BEST improves bed mobility for a client in skeletal leg traction?
questions.rationale: An overhead trapeze helps the client move in bed and on and off the bedpan.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q605 (PDF p. 816)
questions.quote: The use of an overhead trapeze is extremely helpful for assisting a client with moving about in bed

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which parent plan to prevent childhood obesity needs correction?
questions.rationale: Food is not used as a reward. Consistent meal and snack times and no eating while watching TV are encouraged.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q606 (PDF p. 817)
questions.quote: These measures include not using food as a reward

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How should an older client with Parkinson's tremors instill eye drops?
options: Lie down on a bed to instill
questions.rationale: Tremors make instillation hard; lying down gives stability and helps the drops reach the eye.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q608 (PDF p. 820)
questions.quote: The older client is instructed to lie down on a bed or sofa to instill the eye drops

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A client with recurrent trichomoniasis asks about treatment during menses. What is correct?
questions.rationale: Treatment continues through menses because the vagina is more alkaline then and flare-ups are likely.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q614 (PDF p. 827)
questions.quote: Treatment for a recurrent vaginal trichomoniasis infection continues through the menstrual period

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which is a source of histoplasmosis the client should avoid?
questions.rationale: Histoplasmosis comes from soil contaminated with bird (especially chicken and pigeon) and bat droppings. Grape arbors do not harbor it.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q619 (PDF p. 834)
questions.quote: Grape arbors do not harbor the causative organism for histoplasmosis.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: How can women prevent pelvic inflammatory disease?
questions.rationale: Primary prevention of PID is avoiding unprotected intercourse. Douching increases risk.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q625 (PDF p. 842)
questions.quote: The primary prevention of PID includes avoiding unprotected intercourse.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which home instruction is correct for parents of a child being tested for HIV?
questions.rationale: Toothbrushes are not shared, immunizations are kept current, and blood spills are cleaned and rinsed with bleach solution.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q661 (PDF p. 880)
questions.quote: Parents are instructed that toothbrushes are not to be shared.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: When is a post-op NG tube usually removed?
questions.rationale: NG tubes are removed when GI function returns, shown by passing flatus.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q711 (PDF p. 933)
questions.quote: NG tubes are discontinued when normal function returns to the GI tract.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which statement by a teenager treated for an STI needs MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: All sexual contacts must be notified and treated.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q715 (PDF p. 937)
questions.quote: When treating STIs, all sexual contacts must be contacted and treated with medication.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A newly diagnosed diabetic should report glucose that is consistently above which level?
questions.rationale: Normal glucose is 70–110 mg/dL; clients report levels consistently above 250 mg/dL unless the provider says otherwise.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q716 (PDF p. 938)
questions.quote: The normal blood glucose level ranges from 70 to 110 mg/dL (4 to 6 mmol/L)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which student comment about tobacco needs MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: All forms of tobacco, including chewing tobacco, are health hazards.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q732 (PDF p. 957)
questions.quote: All forms of tobacco use, including chewing tobacco, are health hazards.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Why should NICU parents wash their hands properly?
questions.rationale: Proper handwashing by staff and parents prevents nursery infections and lets parents take part in care.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q734 (PDF p. 959)
questions.quote: Appropriate hand washing by staff and parents has been effective for the prevention of nosocomial infections

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: After a month of TB drugs, which finding shows isolation is no longer needed?
questions.rationale: A negative sputum culture shows treatment is effective and the client is no longer infectious.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q736 (PDF p. 961)
questions.quote: A negative culture indicates the effectiveness of treatment.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: What is the BEST advice to a coach for preventing dehydration in hot weather?
questions.rationale: Hot weather speeds fluid and electrolyte loss, so fluid breaks every 30 minutes are scheduled.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q742 (PDF p. 969)
questions.quote: the nurse encourages the coach to schedule fluid breaks at 30-minute intervals

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which menu fits a low-fat diet?
questions.rationale: Skinless turkey, boiled rice, and strawberries are low in fat. Avocado, mayonnaise, butter, and red meat add fat.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q743 (PDF p. 971)
questions.quote: Turkey breast without the skin, boiled rice, and strawberries offer the client nourishing foods that are low in fat.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which food should a client with uric acid stones eliminate?
questions.rationale: Organ meats, sardines, herring, and other high-purine foods are eliminated.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q745 (PDF p. 973)
questions.quote: Organ meats, sardines, herring, and other high-purine foods are eliminated from the diet.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A tuberculin skin test is given Monday. When should it be read?
questions.rationale: The test is read in 48 to 72 hours.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q748 (PDF p. 977)
questions.quote: The tuberculin skin test for tuberculosis is read in 48 to 72 hours

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which home instruction after knee arthroscopy is correct?
questions.rationale: Signs of infection are reported; strenuous exercise is avoided for a few days, but walking is usually allowed.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q773 (PDF p. 1003)
questions.quote: After arthroscopy, signs/symptoms of infection should be reported

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which drink is safe for a client with hiatal hernia?
questions.rationale: Tomato and citrus products irritate, and caffeine increases gastric acid. Apple juice is safe.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q782 (PDF p. 1012)
questions.quote: Substances that are irritating to the client with hiatal hernia include tomato products and citrus fruits

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which food choice shows a client with atherosclerosis understands the diet?
questions.rationale: The diet is low in saturated fat with less red meat and more fruits and vegetables.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q786 (PDF p. 1016)
questions.quote: To lower the risk of heart disease, the diet should be low in saturated fat

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which snack is BEST for a client with hypertension?
questions.rationale: Fresh vegetables like carrots and celery are naturally low in sodium.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q788 (PDF p. 1018)
questions.quote: Fresh fruits and vegetables such as carrots and celery are naturally lower in sodium.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After bronchoscopy, which statement shows the client needs MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: Smoking is avoided. Bright red expectorated blood is reported.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q799 (PDF p. 1029)
questions.quote: The client needs to avoid smoking.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Why does a shy client need extra support for a voiding cystourethrogram?
options: She must void in front of others
questions.rationale: Voiding in the presence of others is embarrassing and may interfere with voiding.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q802 (PDF p. 1035)
questions.quote: Having to void in the presence of others can be very embarrassing for clients

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which explanation BEST eases anxiety about a 12-lead ECG?
questions.rationale: ECG electrodes are painless; the test takes under 5 minutes and requires lying still.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q805 (PDF p. 1039)
questions.quote: The ECG uses painless electrodes that are applied to the chest and limbs.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with hyperparathyroidism says, 'This diet is too hard for me.' What is the BEST response?
questions.rationale: Paraphrasing encourages the client to express feelings and shows the message was understood.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q810 (PDF p. 1044)
questions.quote: By paraphrasing the client’s statement, the nurse can encourage the client to verbalize emotions.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A retiree yells in the dining room that the turkey is dry and cold. What is BEST?
questions.rationale: Asking the client to come to the kitchen respects control, removes him from the room, and allows assessment.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q817 (PDF p. 1051)
questions.quote: Asking the client to accompany the nurse to the kitchen respects the client’s need for control

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: During Allen's test, a client asks, 'No one else did that!' What is MOST therapeutic?
questions.rationale: Allen's test checks collateral circulation before a radial ABG; giving information is therapeutic.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q819 (PDF p. 1053)
questions.quote: Allen’s test is performed to assess collateral circulation in the hand

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client says nurses never answer his light and don't care. Which response is empathetic?
options: 'It's hard to have to ask for help.'
questions.rationale: Empathy is perceiving how the client feels and what it means to him.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q821 (PDF p. 1056)
questions.quote: “Empathy” is a term that describes the nurse’s capacity to enter into the life of another person

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Family of a client who attempted suicide are tearful. What is MOST helpful?
options: 'I'll check when you can see her.'
questions.rationale: Addressing feelings shows empathy. The others are communication blocks: wrong timing, cliché, false reassurance.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q829 (PDF p. 1065)
questions.quote: Option 4 addresses the family’s feelings and displays empathy.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with hives worries about her wedding next week. Which response uses reflection?
questions.rationale: Reflection returns the client's feelings. The others minimize fears or change the focus.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q833 (PDF p. 1069)
questions.quote: The therapeutic communication technique that the nurse uses in option 1 is reflection.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What should preoperative teaching for radical neck dissection focus on FIRST?
questions.rationale: Teaching starts by finding out what the client already knows, to correct misinformation and set a starting point.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q871 (PDF p. 1108)
questions.quote: The first step in client teaching is establishing what the client already knows.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: An older client with a hip fracture has periods of confusion. Which outcome MOST improves cognition?
questions.rationale: Being able to concentrate and take part in care lets the nurse work toward other outcomes.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q899 (PDF p. 1142)
questions.quote: The client needs to be able to concentrate and participate in her or his care.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client on TPN fears lipids will make her obese. What should the nurse do FIRST?
questions.rationale: The comment needs more than information at first; the nurse explores how illness affects self-concept.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q905 (PDF p. 1148)
questions.quote: this client’s comment requires more than a simple informational response initially.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which statement shows POSITIVE coping with chemotherapy hair loss?
questions.rationale: Positive coping identifies feelings and plans interventions for side effects.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q913 (PDF p. 1156)
questions.quote: the client must identify personal feelings and positive interventions to deal with side effects.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A daughter feels guilty that her grieving father developed DKA despite her care. What is BEST?
questions.rationale: Environment, infection, or emotional stress such as grief can trigger DKA, which eases misplaced guilt.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q914 (PDF p. 1157)
questions.quote: Environment, infection, or an emotional stressor can initiate the physiological mechanism of DKA.
